title: Delete Cancelled Orders
statement:
An online shop is cleaning up its orders table. Cancelled orders will never ship, so remove them, then list the orders that are left.

The `orders` table has these columns:

- `id`: the order number, the primary key
- `customer`: the customer's name
- `status`: one of `pending`, `shipped`, `delivered`, or `cancelled`
- `total`: the order total in dollars

Delete every order whose status is `cancelled`. Then return `id`, `customer`, `status`, and `total` for every remaining order, ordered by `id`.

Expected output:

```text
DELETE 3

  id  |   customer    |  status   | total
------+---------------+-----------+--------
 1001 | Laura Mendes  | delivered |  54.90
 1003 | Mia Johansson | shipped   |  18.75
 1005 | Laura Mendes  | pending   | 230.40
 1006 | Tom Becker    | delivered |  75.00
(4 rows)
```
setup:
CREATE TABLE orders (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  customer TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL,
  total NUMERIC(8, 2) NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO orders (id, customer, status, total) VALUES
  (1001, 'Laura Mendes', 'delivered', 54.90),
  (1002, 'Kofi Asante', 'cancelled', 120.00),
  (1003, 'Mia Johansson', 'shipped', 18.75),
  (1004, 'Raj Malhotra', 'cancelled', 9.99),
  (1005, 'Laura Mendes', 'pending', 230.40),
  (1006, 'Tom Becker', 'delivered', 75.00),
  (1007, 'Kofi Asante', 'cancelled', 42.50);
